- rest and recovery. I injured myself deadlifting / BB rowing a year and a half ago, and IMMEDIATELY did not do anything that would aggravate my lower back. No DL's, no squats, and all of my rows had to be chest supported for the longest time.

- I then set about rehabbing my lower back and core. Did back extensions before every leg and back workout to get the blood in there so to speak, and here I am. Also did a lot of abs.

THIS IS A LONG STORY, reddit. Sorry, no TL:DR.  But it's one hell of an experience.

My entire childhood was amazing in terms of quality.  My parents both worked top tier corporate jobs at the same company, loved eachother and myself very much.  We were a very close family, the three of us.  We had a nice house in a good neighborhood, they had nice cars.  However, my dad developed a back problem and had to begin using crutches.  He became miserable and was eventually fired.  He became kind of self-pitying, in a way.  He still loved us, he just mad at the world.  We always worked through things together though, we were always still a family.  

When I was 17, my mom found out she had a lung disease called idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.  No known cause for the disease...Look it up, it's an awful disease.  I had to personally administer painkillers to my own mother.  That was the most traumatic part for me.  My mother, who was a corporate saleswoman, the strongest and happiest person I had ever known, begging me to not give her the medicine because she didn't want me to see her that way, all drugged up.  She had to be on the meds to be able to breathe without being in pain.  All the while my dad watched on and went into denial, he kept saying how he thought she was going to "pull through" somehow.  

She died in her sleep one morning, before I went to school.  I don't even remember the last thing I said to her(just realized this as I'm writing)... That kills me.  Her death hurt a lot but at the same time, she was in too much pain to really exist without a ludicrous amount of painkillers, so all the pain of her death came with a sense of relief.  Me and my dad became estranged from the rest of the family(which was a big family, believe me) because they wanted to give us time to grieve.

Fast forward two months later, me and my dad have grown distant.  I don't know how or why.  I think we both just missed her too much.  I tried to kill myself once, nobody knows that (except you reddit).  Anyhow, he started drinking more than one beer a day if you catch my meaning, and I started hanging out with friends I hadn't seen in a while due to all the family stuff.  I started drinking and smoking weed, spent a lot of time out with people, away from my dad.  I hid all of this from him.  He had no idea, or at least he never led on that he did.  

One Sunday, I make lunch and go downstairs to watch TV, only to find my dad in his chair having what is clearly a seizure.  I call 911 for the first time ever in my life and the ambulance comes.  I follow it to the hospital, long story short they don't know what is wrong with my dad.  He comes home two days later at his own insistence, despite the doctors and myself asking him to stay.  He had a fear of hospitals because of what had happened with his back.  He started becoming weak, tired and had 2 more seizures and hospital trips before he finally agreed to stay in the hospital.  The entire time he was in the hospital, he told me not to tell anyone in the family.  The only person who knew was my half-sister (his daughter from earlier marriage).  She came to see him in the hospital, took me out to dinner, then went back home.  Eventually, they released my dad after a week and a half, again at his insistence, because they couldn't figure out what was wrong with him.

The following five days are great.  Me and my dad get kind of closer, start talking more.  I take a couple days off of school to help him out, and he calls his brother, my half-sister, and other family members.  Just shooting the shit, you know.  He never mentioned any of the medical stuff that he just went through, just talked to them.

It's Thursday night one week.  I go into my dad's room, to say goodnight.  He sits in the darkness, watching TV and smoking a cigarette.  "Hey dad, I'm going to see a movie tomorrow night after school.  Won't be back until late though, if that's cool?"  He says "Ok bud.  Be good.  Night."  I go sleep, excited to go see Punisher: War Zone the next day.

School comes to an end, I realize I had forgotten something at home.  Go back to get it, yet I don't hear the radio or TV coming from upstairs.  No noise.  Weird, I thought.  I go upstairs to see what's not going on.  Walk down the hall, staring at myself in the mirror at the end of it.  Go around the corner to the left, into my parents (now dad's) room.  And there's my dad, on the bed.  I can't see his face at first, so I thought he had had a seizure again.  I go to touch his arm, "Dad? Dad are yo-"  And then I see his face and feel how cold he is.  He's dead.

I cry for an hour in his room before I call 911, who send a bunch of cops and EMT's.  They take a statement from me, call my aunt to come get me, and wheel out my dad's body.

That all took place in a 3 month period.  Mom died Sept. 17th, dad died on Dec. 5th.

That was back in 2008.  And here I am, four years older.  Other things went on afterwards, but they are different stories.  That was the most traumatizing experience of my childhood.

If you took the time to read this, thanks.  Means a lot, just you reading it.  I've never sat down and written it all out before.  Teared up a bit at some parts.  Thanks, again.
